questions.text: According to the passage, which of the following best describes an implicit assumption in an argument?

options.label: A
options.text: A stated reason supporting the claim.

options.label: B
options.text: An unstated belief necessary for the argument to hold.

options.label: C
options.text: A counterargument presented for refutation.

options.label: D
options.text: A statistical evidence cited by the author.

questions.solution: Correct answer: An unstated belief necessary for the argument to hold..

questions.text: A candidate encounters an inference question where one option is factually true in the real world but not supported by the passage. According to the Principle of Passage‑Only Reasoning, how should this option be treated?

options.label: A
options.text: Select it because it is factually correct

options.label: B
options.text: Eliminate it because answers must be grounded exclusively in the passage

options.label: C
options.text: Select it if it aligns with the candidate's domain knowledge

options.label: D
options.text: Mark it as correct only if the passage does not contradict it

questions.solution: Correct answer: Eliminate it because answers must be grounded exclusively in the passage.

questions.text: Paragraph 1 cites a single study showing a 12% rise in test scores after a policy change. Paragraph 3 reveals the study had a small sample and short duration. The author concludes the policy is universally effective. This conclusion is:

options.label: A
options.text: Supported by the evidence presented.

options.label: B
options.text: Weakened by the omitted limitations noted later.

options.label: C
options.text: Irrelevant to the study’s findings.

options.label: D
options.text: Strengthened by the later paragraph’s details.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Weakened by the omitted limitations noted later..

questions.text: A delivery company employs a driver who, while delivering a parcel, assaults the recipient because of a personal grudge unrelated to the delivery. The company’s policy prohibits violence. Applying the “course of employment” test for vicarious liability, is the company liable?

options.label: A
options.text: Yes, because the assault occurred during working hours and at the delivery location.

options.label: B
options.text: Yes, because the risk of assault is inherent in the business of serving the public.

options.label: C
options.text: No, because the assault was a frolic — a personal act not a mode of performing the authorised task.

options.label: D
options.text: No, because the company had a policy prohibiting violence, which negates vicarious liability.

questions.solution: Correct answer: No, because the assault was a frolic — a personal act not a mode of performing the authorised task..

questions.text: Which of the following best defines the 'Almost Right' trap as described in the passage's section on Diagnostic Answer-Option Forensics?

options.label: A
options.text: An option that uses high-frequency passage vocabulary to exploit familiarity heuristic

options.label: B
options.text: An option that contains a verifiably true statement from the passage but fails the question's specific demand

options.label: C
options.text: An option that applies a statutory interpretation canon outside its proper jurisdictional domain

options.label: D
options.text: An option that infers causation from a historical correlation without corroborating evidence

questions.solution: Correct answer: An option that contains a verifiably true statement from the passage but fails the question's specific demand.

questions.text: In Keshav Singh v. Speaker, Legislative Assembly (1965), the Supreme Court established which principle regarding legislative privileges?

options.label: A
options.text: The House is the sole and final judge of its own privileges

options.label: B
options.text: Judicial review extends to examining whether a claimed privilege is consistent with the Constitution

options.label: C
options.text: Legislative privileges are absolute and cannot be questioned in any court

options.label: D
options.text: Privileges under Article 105 are subject to the President's prior approval

questions.solution: Correct answer: Judicial review extends to examining whether a claimed privilege is consistent with the Constitution.

questions.text: A state enacts a law that completely bans the sale of a certain chemical to protect public health. The government argues the ban pursues a legitimate aim and is rationally connected to that aim. However, a licensing regime with strict safety standards would achieve the same objective while imposing a lesser restriction on the right to trade. Under the four‑step proportionality test, at which step does the law fail?

options.label: A
options.text: Legitimate aim

options.label: B
options.text: Rational connection

options.label: C
options.text: Necessity

options.label: D
options.text: Proportionality stricto sensu

questions.text: The passage lists several common traps in advanced reading comprehension. Which of the following is explicitly identified as a trap?

options.label: A
options.text: Confusing the author's tone with the tone of a cited expert.

options.label: B
options.text: Over-inferring from limited evidence.

options.label: C
options.text: Failing to identify the main idea of each paragraph.

options.label: D
options.text: Misreading complex vocabulary.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Over-inferring from limited evidence..

questions.text: Which body explicitly names the lead agency for a United Nations International Year?

options.label: A
options.text: The UN Secretariat.

options.label: B
options.text: The General Assembly through its resolution.

options.label: C
options.text: The Economic and Social Council (ECOSOC).

options.label: D
options.text: The Secretary‑General.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The General Assembly through its resolution..

questions.text: The government issues a press release stating that it will provide a 20 % subsidy to manufacturers of solar panels. Relying on this announcement, a company invests ₹5 crore in a new production line. Before any formal notification or scheme is published, the government withdraws the announcement. The company claims a legitimate expectation. What factual element is essential for the claim to succeed?

options.label: A
options.text: The announcement must be made in a formal gazette notification.

options.label: B
options.text: The company must have suffered a detriment as a result of its reliance on the representation.

options.label: C
options.text: The government must have acted in bad faith when withdrawing the announcement.

options.label: D
options.text: The subsidy must be a statutory entitlement rather than a discretionary policy.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The company must have suffered a detriment as a result of its reliance on the representation..

questions.text: Which of the following correctly matches the South African capital city with its governmental function?

options.label: A
options.text: Pretoria – Legislative; Cape Town – Executive; Bloemfontein – Judicial

options.label: B
options.text: Pretoria – Executive; Cape Town – Legislative; Bloemfontein – Judicial

options.label: C
options.text: Pretoria – Judicial; Cape Town – Executive; Bloemfontein – Legislative

options.label: D
options.text: Pretoria – Executive; Cape Town – Judicial; Bloemfontein – Legislative

questions.solution: Correct answer: Pretoria – Executive; Cape Town – Legislative; Bloemfontein – Judicial.
